sections.html:
Gates owners can hire an agent, go it alone, or take a cash offer from someone who buys the house as it stands. Gates is a town in Monroe County and a suburb of Rochester, so the town hall, the Monroe County Clerk and the county's tax portal handle most of the paperwork.

A fast sale mostly depends on clean records. In Gates that means a current Compliance Certificate for any work done, a tax payoff figure and the right school district named on the bill.

Gates is a mostly owner-occupied suburb that borders Rochester on its east side. About 91% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so many owners have stayed a long time and may be selling a house with original systems. A pre-listing walk-through can show what a buyer's inspector will raise.

Residents commute an average of 17.5 minutes. Interstate 390 curves through the east, Interstate 490 crosses the middle, and Route 531 runs northwest toward Spencerport. Gates-Chili and Spencerport school districts both draw on Gates property, and ZIP codes 14624 and 14606 cover most of the town. Ask your agent or lender how an appraisal could affect a financed buyer before you accept an offer.

The Town of Gates completed a town-wide reassessment in 2025, and the Assessor's page now lists a 2026 final tax assessment roll. The assessed value on a tax bill is therefore recent and tied to current market value.

The assessor's office compares each property to nearby sales and adjusts values when a building permit shows new construction, remodeling or demolition. The assessment funds the town, Monroe County, the school district and special district charges such as the fire and ambulance districts. The calendar runs on a fixed cycle:

  • March 1: taxable status date, and the exemption filing deadline.
  • May 1: tentative roll filed and grievance forms become available.
  • Fourth Tuesday in May: Grievance Day before the Board of Assessment Review, which has five resident members.
  • July 1: final roll filed, with decisions mailed by that date.

The Board can only hear valuation complaints, not tax complaints, so check whether the assessed value or an exemption is the problem before you file.

Gates owners receive two bills a year. The Town and County bill covers a calendar year and the school bill covers July 1 to June 30. The Tax Receiver's office is at 1605 Buffalo Road. Because penalties rise month by month, a seller who is behind should get a written payoff figure before setting a closing date. After May 31, collection moves to the Monroe County Treasurer.

  • Town and County bill: mailed around the turn of the year, with full payment due by February 10 to avoid interest.
  • Late rates: interest begins at 1.5% from February 11 and climbs to 6% by May.
  • School bill: mailed so it arrives in early September, with full payment due by October 1.

The Tax Receiver's office accepts cash, check and card, though a card payment adds a fee. Bill pay can take up to 14 days and arrive without a postmark, so send it early.

The Town of Gates website carries most of the forms you may need while preparing a sale, and its Town Code is posted online.

  • Code complaints: the town accepts a code or dog complaint through an online form.
  • Electrical work: the town keeps a list of approved electrical inspectors, which helps if a buyer wants electrical work signed off.
  • Yard debris: a pickup schedule is posted online, and a refuse hauler list is available.
  • Fire and ambulance: special district charges for the Gates Fire Department and Gates Volunteer Ambulance are based on assessed value.

The Gates Building Department reviews plans, issues permits for decks, pools, additions and signs, and issues Compliance Certificates. Zoning questions go to the same office, and a Zoning Compliance Request carries a $75 fee. The Zoning Board of Appeals meets the second Monday of each month for variance requests.

After closing, the Monroe County Clerk, who acts as registrar of deeds and mortgages, records the deed at 39 W. Main Street, Room 101 in Rochester. New York charges a seller's transfer tax of $2 per $500 of price, and the TP-584 form goes in with the deed. The Monroe County Real Property Portal shows tax bills and sales histories for parcels.

Ask the Building Department for a printout of permits on the parcel, and confirm that the Assessor's records match the house as it stands today.

sections.h2: A cash sale in Gates, step by step
sections.html:
Gather your Compliance Certificates, latest Town and County and school bills, and the permit printout. Share them with the buyer at the first walk-through so the offer reflects what the house is, not what the buyer fears. After you accept, the title search turns up liens or tax balances, and payoffs come out of your proceeds at closing.

Closing includes recording the deed with the Monroe County Clerk and filing the TP-584 return. Because the school and Town and County bills run on different calendars, expect your attorney to prorate whichever one is open on closing day.

faqs.q: What is a Compliance Certificate in Gates?
faqs.a: A document the town Building Department issues after required permits and inspections are complete. Buyers' attorneys often ask for it when a seller added a deck, pool or alteration, so confirm yours is on file.

faqs.q: When is the Gates tax bill due without interest?
faqs.a: Full payment of the Town and County bill is due by February 10. Interest begins on February 11 at 1.5% and rises through May, and payments after May 31 go to the Monroe County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Gates house in?
faqs.a: Gates property falls within either the Gates-Chili Central School District or the Spencerport Central School District. Your tax bill names the district, and the Assessor's Office can confirm it.

faqs.q: Can I challenge my Gates assessment after the 2025 reassessment?
faqs.a: Yes. File the grievance form with the Assessor by the fourth Tuesday in May, and the Board of Assessment Review decides by July 1. Bring sales of similar nearby homes as evidence.

faqs.q: Where is the deed recorded for a Gates house?
faqs.a: At the Monroe County Clerk's office in downtown Rochester, which keeps deeds, mortgages and liens. The office keeps weekday hours from nine to five.
